Container.Name: Caretaker-Hub
Container.Overview: Self-hosted Moonlight/Apollo companion: wake a Windows gaming PC (Wake-on-LAN), unlock the lock screen from your phone, and sleep it when you are done. LAN-only — do not expose to the internet.
Container.Requires: Host networking is required so Wake-on-LAN and agent discovery (UDP 7843) reach your LAN. Keep this container off the public internet — use Tailscale/WireGuard if you need remote access. See SAFETY.md in the project repo.
Container.Description:
Caretaker Hub runs on your Unraid box and talks to a small Windows agent on your gaming PC.
After install: 1. Open the WebUI (or http://TOWER:PORT) and sign in with the UI password you set below. 2. On the Windows PC: Hub → Setup → Download installer → run as Administrator. 3. The installer shows a pairing code. Type it next to the PC under Nearby PCs and tap Pair, then Wake / Unlock / Sleep from your phone.
Uses host networking. If 8080 is taken, set BOTH "WebUI Port" and "CARETAKER_PORT" to the same free port (e.g. 8060). The WebUI button follows WebUI Port.
Not malware, but privileged: anyone who can log into the Hub can wake, unlock, and sleep paired PCs. Full details: https://github.com/TRU5T/caretaker/blob/main/SAFETY.md

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Persistent Hub config (password hash, hosts, agent tokens, pinned agent certificates). Owner-only permissions.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port used by Unraid's WebUI button. With host networking this is not a Docker port-map — set CARETAKER_PORT to the SAME number so the Hub listens here.

Config.Name: CARETAKER_PORT
Config.Description: Port the Hub process binds on the Unraid host. Must match WebUI Port (e.g. both 8060).

Config.Name: UI Password
Config.Description: Hub login password (10+ characters). Used only on first start (when config.json is created). If left empty it is changeme and the Hub forces you to change it at first sign-in.

Config.Name: Session Secret
Config.Description: Optional HMAC secret for session cookies (32+ characters, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32). Leave empty to let the Hub generate one and keep it in appdata. Short or example values are ignored. Changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: Run as UID
Config.Description: The container starts as root only to fix appdata ownership, then runs the Hub as this user (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: Run as GID
Config.Description: Group for the Hub process (100 = users).
